transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. 

Um, the main reason I came in is that I just get pulled off track so easily. Like, it just takes one Slack ping, or hearing a song lyric, or even just a random idea for another project popping into my head, and... suddenly I’ve completely lost the thread of the dashboard I was actually supposed to be finishing. It's just getting really frustrating to deal with.
When you find yourself getting pulled off track, do you notice that your mind is preoccupied with persistent, excessive worries about everyday life events or responsibilities?

No, not really. It's not that I'm worrying about things. Like, I'm not sitting there stressing out about my classes or life in general. It's more just... my mind wanders to whatever else is happening around me, or just random thoughts, rather than feeling anxious or preoccupied with responsibilities.
Do you often feel like you have an internal 'motor' that makes it difficult for you to sit still for long periods, such as during meetings or while watching a movie?

Yeah, I definitely feel that way. Even on days when I don’t have classes or a formal schedule, I can't really just sit around and do nothing. I’ll jump from editing a prototype for a project, to cleaning my desk, to opening up a new dataset to look at. It's like... resting just feels weird to me unless I’m actively doing something.

When you are in situations that require you to remain seated for long periods, such as in a classroom or a long meeting, do you find that you frequently fidget with your hands or feet, or do you often feel the need to get up and leave your seat?

Yeah, definitely. When I'm in long meetings or, like, portfolio reviews for my major, I'm almost always doing something like that. I'll be bouncing my leg, clicking a pen, twisting my rings around, or just shifting in my chair a lot. Honestly, I don't even realize I'm doing it half the time until I notice someone looking at me.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others when they are speaking, or do you frequently find it difficult to wait your turn in conversations or group activities?

Yeah, I do. Especially when people are brainstorming for a project. I’ll just... blurt out my idea, or I'll start adding things to their Figma board before they’ve even finished explaining what they're doing. I just get really excited about the idea, but I can tell afterward that I probably came off as a bit pushy. It's just hard for me to wait my turn to jump in.
Looking back at your childhood, say before you were 12 years old, do you remember having these same difficulties with staying focused on tasks or sitting still?

Yeah, I do. It's been like this for a long time. Even back in elementary school, my teachers used to write comments on my report cards about me rushing through worksheets or losing track of directions. They also mentioned I'd talk over my classmates a lot during group work. And at home, my parents actually had to sit right beside me while I did my homework. If they didn't, I would just wander off or start doing something else before I was actually finished.
Have these challenges with focus, restlessness, and impulsivity impacted your life in more than one area, such as both your academic performance and your personal relationships or social life?

Yes, it definitely affects more than just one area. Academically and professionally, it's caused some real issues. I've actually lost a few small freelance contracts, and I missed out on a big portfolio competition recently. It just comes down to people not being able to rely on me to follow through cleanly or finish things on time. And socially, it spills over there too. Some of my friends and classmates are pretty hesitant to work with me on group projects now. They tell me they like my ideas, but the actual collaboration part is just too frustrating for them because I'm so disorganized and impulsive.
